accepted_claims: For all integers b>=1 and k>=0, every b-iatlon graph on at least bk+1 vertices has a constrained K_{1,k}; p(K_{1,k},b)=bk+1. General sharp-star theorem and monotone-system coloring proof credited to Ferudun (2026).

The star upper bound transfers to closure drawings under the (b+1)-point path-component pair condition. The finite compact-slab example proves Euclidean closure sharpness in every dimension d>=1, including the plane.

Paták's join mechanism with the sharp-star theorem gives p(K_1+F,b)<=b p(F,b)+1 and the credited complete-graph upper bound p(K_n,b)<=sum_{j=0}^{n-1}b^j. For arbitrary b-iatlon graphs, R(n,b+1)<=p(K_n,b); this Ramsey encoding need not be planar-closure realizable.

The directly checked closure lower bound for K_n is (n-1)b+1. The same join recurrence yields p(K_{m,n},b)<=n b^m+sum_{j=0}^{m-1}b^j, including p(K_{3,3},3)<=94; these are credited consequences, not claimed new theorems.
